headline: Advances in Quantum Error Correction & Sensing
summary: Today's research explores fundamental and practical frontiers in quantum information, spanning disordered noise decoding, optimal parameter estimation, and ultra-fast FPGA hardware for real-time error correction. Together, these studies address the critical bottleneck of managing noise and decoding latency in scalable quantum systems.

themes.title: Quantum Error Correction and Decoding
themes.body: New theoretical and hardware frameworks advance how quantum error correction handles complex noise and real-time processing constraints. Studies investigate information-theoretic limits under disordered noise and introduce sub-microsecond FPGA-based neural decoders for surface codes.

themes.title: Quantum Sensing and Hamiltonian Estimation
themes.body: Recent work establishes optimal precision bounds for quantum sensing with time-dependent Hamiltonians in the presence of Markovian noise and nuisance parameters, revealing distinct strategies for noise suppression versus parameter handling.

connections.body: Both works tackle the challenge of mitigating adverse physical effects in quantum architectures—specifically addressing how to handle unknown or disordered noise distributions during decoding and parameter estimation.
